description: STRENGTHENING HEALTH INFORMATION SYSTEM IN SOUTH SUDAN - SOUTH SUDAN, AFRICA’S NEWEST COUNTRY, IS RECOVERING FROM A PROTRACTED CIVIL WAR AND HAS MULTIPLE HEALTH AND HUMANITARIAN NEEDS, INCLUDING A GENERALIZED HIV EPIDEMIC. SINCE 2010, NEW HIV INFECTIONS IN SOUTH SUDAN INCREASED 15% AND AIDS-RELATED DEATHS DECREASED 15%. HIV CASE IDENTIFICATION, ACCESS TO TREATMENT, AND CONTINUITY IN CARE ARE SUBOPTIMAL. SOUTH SUDAN HAS LIMITED CAPACITY TO PROVIDE ESSENTIAL HEALTH SERVICES TO ITS POPULATION, INCLUDING INTERNALLY DISPLACED PEOPLE AND RETURNEES. DONORS AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS (NGOS) HAVE BEEN PROVIDING MOST HIV/TB AND OTHER HEALTH SERVICES, WHICH HAS LED TO MANY ACCOMPLISHMENTS YET HAS ALSO FOSTERED DONOR-LED AND DISPARATE SYSTEMS AND STRUCTURES. STRENGTHENING THE NATIONAL HEALTH SYSTEM, INCLUDING THE HEALTH INFORMATION SYSTEM (HIS), AND EQUIPPING THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH (MOH) TO LEAD AND OWN A NATIONALLY UNIFIED HIV/TB RESPONSE TO ACCELERATE EPIDEMIC CONTROL IS CRITICAL. SUPPORT FROM THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION (CDC), PRESIDENT’S EMERGENCY PLAN FOR AIDS RELIEF (PEPFAR), IMPLEMENTING PARTNERS (IPS), AND STAKEHOLDERS HAS STRENGTHENED SOUTH SUDAN’S HIV/TB RESPONSE. YET MANY CHALLENGES REMAIN, INCLUDING SCARCE WORKFORCE CAPACITY, PARALLEL DATA SYSTEMS, LIMITED AND POOR-QUALITY PATIENT-LEVEL DATA COLLECTION AND USE, LACK OF A FUNCTIONING, INTEROPERABLE HIS, AND LIMITED DISEASE SURVEILLANCE CAPACITY. BUILDING MOH CAPACITY TO GENERATE, ANALYZE, AND USE STRATEGIC INFORMATION (SI) AT NATIONAL AND SUBNATIONAL LEVELS IS CRITICAL TO IMPROVE PATIENT CARE AND EPIDEMIC CONTROL. ICAP HAS THE EXPERIENCE AND EXPERTISE TO DELIVER TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE (TA) AND CAPACITY BUILDING (CB) THAT GOES BEYOND THE DOMAIN OF HIS FOR AN INTEGRATED, PERSON-CENTERED, WHOLE-OF-SYSTEM APPROACH. OUR APPROACH IS DESIGNED TO ACHIEVE FULL NATIONAL OWNERSHIP OF PROJECT INTERVENTIONS INCLUDING AN INTEROPERABLE HIS. WE WILL SUPPORT THE MOH TO GENERATE QUALITY DATA FOR DECISION-MAKING THROUGH INTEGRATED AND REINFORCING TA AND MULTI-MODAL CAPACITY-CB AT NATIONAL, STATE, COUNTY, AND HF LEVELS. ICAP’S EFFORTS PRIORITIZE PERSON-CENTERED HIV MONITORING AND PRACTICAL, SCALABLE, AND SUSTAINABLE SI SOLUTIONS. WE WILL LEVERAGE OUR STRONG PARTNERSHIPS AND KNOWLEDGE OF THE HEALTH SYSTEM ACROSS THE CLINICAL CASCADE TO IMPLEMENT A SECURE, STANDARD BASED, INTEROPERABLE HEALTH DATA SYSTEM AND ONE MONITORING SYSTEM UNDER MOH LEADERSHIP FOR A COUNTRY LED AND OWNED HIV/TB RESPONSE. ICAP IS AN HIV/TB GLOBAL THOUGHT LEADER AND TRUSTED IP TO PEPFAR/CDC AND MOH IN OVER 30 COUNTRIES. IN SOUTH SUDAN WE HAVE A DECADE OF EXPERIENCE WORKING ACROSS THE HIV/TB CLINICAL CASCADE IN PARTNERSHIP WITH MOH AND STAKEHOLDERS. OUR EXPERIENCED SOUTH SUDAN TEAM (99% LOCAL), BOLSTERED BY ICAP’S GLOBAL TEAM OF SI/HIS EXPERTS, IS READY ON DAY ONE TO PROVIDE RAPID AND EFFECTIVE SUPPORT TO MOH TO GENERATE QUALITY HEALTH DATA FOR INFORMED DECISION MAKING AND ACCELERATE MOH OWNERSHIP OF AN INFORMED HIV/TB RESPONSE.

cfda_info.cfda_objectives: The U.S. President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) is the U.S. Government initiative to help save the lives of those suffering from HIV/AIDS around the world. This historic commitment is the largest by any nation to combat a single disease internationally, and PEPFAR investments also help alleviate suffering from other diseases across the global health spectrum.   PEPFAR is the cornerstone and largest component of the U.S. President’s Global Health Initiative. With a special focus on improving the health of women, newborns and children, the Global Health Initiative’s goal is to save the greatest number of lives by increasing and building upon what works and, then, supporting countries as they work to improve the health of their own people.

To assist States and political subdivisions of States in meeting the cost of establishing and maintaining Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) prevention and surveillance programs.

To continue and strengthen effective human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) programs and to affect, maintain, measure and evaluate the extent of HIV/AIDS incidence and prevalence throughout the United States and its territories, providing information for targeting and implementing HIV prevention and surveillance activities.
